summary: Turn 21. The map clarification was accepted (audit_spec_version 6) and the confirmed violation CLM-DURABLE-BAL stands (confirmed=true, outcome=violated, no blockers); pending_work is empty. With the run near its time boundary I added one more sourced core question rather than starting a chain that could not finish. New source S-QUORUM-SIZES covers replica/replica.go:121-135: FastQuorumSize() = F + (F+1)/2 and SlowQuorumSize() = (N+1)/2, with F taken from the deployment as (len(ReplicaAddrs)-1)/2. For odd N these coincide with the expected EPaxos fast quorum and a majority, but for even N they do not — N=4 gives F=1, FastQuorumSize=2 and SlowQuorumSize=2, so two fast quorums of size 2 can be disjoint and a slow quorum of 2 is not a majority of 4. Since handlePreAcceptReply fast-commits on preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize()-1 (epaxos/epaxos.go:926-946) and handlePrepareReply rebuilds an instance once SlowQuorumSize() Prepare replies arrive (epaxos/epaxos.go:1210-1218), the size of the deciding sets would matter if even N were admissible. Submitted action=continue with a new Candidate (disposition needs_specific_evidence, preferred_check source_review, priority 2; activity_classes A1 with A3 support; principal fact F-DECISION, direct behavior B-PREACCEPT-REPLY-LEADER, supporting B-PREPARE-REPLY-LEADER and B-ACCEPT-REPLY-LEADER; obligation_relation_kind establishment). The applicability premise is explicit and unresolved rather than assumed: the captured deployment examples use odd replica counts, nothing in the captured files validates that N is odd at startup, and the slow path's explicit majority check (acceptOKs+1 > N/2) may or may not compensate. Counterevidence and unknowns state all three open points (whether N is validated odd, whether allEqual plus the initial-ballot condition make non-intersecting fast quorums safe, and whether recovery's Accept phase restores the majority requirement). This is kept as a separate question from the confirmed durability finding. Preflight validation returns valid=true; acceptance and any execution remain the controller's.
